agent_trace.summary: On abdominal CT, the luminal surface of bowel is normally outlined by low-attenuation intraluminal gas or contrast, with the bowel wall seen as a thin enhancing rim after IV contrast. The term commonly used for visible bright lining of the lumen/wall on contrast-enhanced CT is 'mucosal enhancement' or simply 'enhancement' of the bowel wall, depending on the context.

key_facts: The small bowel is commonly identified on abdominal CT by its folded, tubular loops in the mesentery.
Enhancement refers to increased attenuation after contrast administration, usually reflecting vascularized tissue.
A visibly bright luminal-facing lining usually indicates mucosal or inner wall enhancement, not the gas-filled lumen itself.
Normal bowel wall is thin and may enhance mildly and symmetrically when distended and contrasted.
